hook_text: British officers called him one of the most formidable opponents they ever faced. He died a prisoner on Robben Island.
clip_script: Maqoma, son of the Xhosa chief Ngqika, first tried to live alongside the colony, building homes and gardens in the Kat River valley. In 1829 soldiers burnt them and drove his people out. In 1834 he struck back. Then, in 1850, from the dark forests of the Waterkloof and the Amathole mountains, he led a guerrilla war that held off thousands of British troops for months. The British won only by burning crops and starving families. In 1857 he was sent to Robben Island. He died there in 1873, a century before another prisoner, Nelson Mandela, arrived.
visual_style: Misty forested mountains of the Amathole; burnt homesteads in a valley; a lone figure looking out to sea from Robben Island's shore.
pacing: Measured, building through the war, quiet at the end.
